title: FCC Chairman: Regulate Internet Like Public Utility
main_content:
The head of the U.S. Federal Communication Commission called Wednesday for the government to regulate the Internet like a public utility to keep it “fast, fair and open.”

In what is known as “net neutrality,” the proposal would prevent big Internet providers from charging content providers — such as wealthy companies that stream movies online — from being able to pay more to get their product to customers faster than smaller companies.

“My proposal assures the rights of Internet users to go where they want, when they want, and the rights of innovators to introduce new products, without asking anyone’s permission,” FCC Chairman Tom Wheeler wrote in Wired magazine.

Internet providers oppose the plan, saying government regulation would discourage investment.

Net neutrality had been in place before a federal court ruled against it.

FCC commissioners plan to vote on the Wheeler proposal later this month.

questions.question: Why does the head of the FCC want the Internet to be regulated like a public utility?
options: To ensure equal access and speeds for all users regardless of company size
To promote government control over all Internet content
To allow content providers to pay for faster service exclusively
To streamline the approval process for Internet innovations
questions.answer: To ensure equal access and speeds for all users regardless of company size

questions.question: What does the proposal mean?
options: It allows large companies to pay for preferential treatment on the Internet
It seeks to reestablish rules that prevent Internet provider favoritism
It mandates that all Internet data be free from any subscription fees
It encourages competition among Internet providers for pricing
questions.answer: It seeks to reestablish rules that prevent Internet provider favoritism

questions.question: What does Tom Wheeler say about his proposal?
options: It is designed to limit user choices and guide them to preferred content
It prioritizes the rights of users and innovators without needing approval
It will eliminate all forms of content monetization on the Internet
It guarantees that only established companies can introduce new products
questions.answer: It prioritizes the rights of users and innovators without needing approval
